evidence: Not a fault of the replayer's rule 9 and not covered by any row's condition. The failing case is the astral doc's {from: 11, to: 5, skips: [0, 9, 4]} (only 3 astral cases are all-integer; the other two run clean). After next(0) gives "x", the shadow stands at 9 (UTF-16); skip 9 ends at 0, a boundary in both units, so tests/replay/text/host.rs:449-461 (Iter::advance) converts it to 13 bytes and calls Ferrum, as plan.md "Positions" rule 9 says. Inside the cursor, the positive skip of a backward partial cursor is clipped by the forward bound to - pos (mirrors/cm6/state/src/text.ts:507-511; kept by state.cm6.225.d1): 2 units in cm6 (to 11 - pos 9), 2 bytes in Ferrum (15 - 13), a distance measured on [pos, to] and then applied backward over [pos - 2, pos], which holds the break and half of the second emoji. cm6 lands between the surrogates and returns the lone surrogate "\ud83d" (its FlatPartial model, which cm6 matched on all 3200 cases of F7168); Ferrum lands at byte 3 of the line "😀" and panics at src/char.rs:116 (assert_char_boundary via cut, src/text.rs:51-58), which is the panic design.md section 5 (line 117, "the value of a cursor") gives for D1. So Ferrum does cm6's arithmetic in bytes as state.cm6.225.d1 decides; the consequence is the kind Q117 decided for state.cm6.225.d2 (a distance that does not commute with conversion), but d2's condition is a negative skip before the first next, and this is a positive skip after it: no row names this condition, so the attribution could not find one. The same clipping also lands on a boundary elsewhere and returns other text silently (repro 2), which would show as a mismatch with no row. Question raised in the report.
